when: Predicts a nominal outcome with three or more unordered categories, comparing each category against a reference.
example: You predict which of three transport modes (car, bus, bike) a commuter chooses from their age and distance. Multinomial logistic regression compares each mode against a reference mode.
small_sample: Spreading a small sample across several outcome categories leaves sparse cells. Combine rare categories where it makes sense, or use a penalised estimator.
assumptions: The outcome has three or more unordered categories
Independence of irrelevant alternatives is plausible
Adequate cases in every outcome category
alternative: Ordinal logistic regression, when the categories have a natural order

# survey_skeleton.R
# StatChooser sample survey skeleton (surveyframe method = "regression_logistic_multinomial").
# Section A is a standard demographic block. Section B, and C/D/E where present,
# carry the measures the analysis plan needs. Replace every [bracketed] stem
# with your own validated items before fielding the survey.
# install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)

# ---- Choice sets (define once, reuse) ----
agree5 <- sf_choices("agree5", 1:5,
  c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"))
out_cat <- sf_choices("out_cat", 1:3, c("Outcome A", "Outcome B", "Outcome C"))
gender_cs <- sf_choices("gender_cs",
  c("woman", "man", "nonbinary", "selfdescribe", "na"),
  c("Woman", "Man", "Non-binary", "Prefer to self-describe", "Prefer not to say"))
edu_cs <- sf_choices("edu_cs", 1:5,
  c("Secondary or below", "Diploma", "Bachelor degree", "Master degree", "Doctorate"))
role_cs <- sf_choices("role_cs", 1:4,
  c("Entry or junior", "Mid-level", "Senior or manager", "Executive or owner"))
industry_cs <- sf_choices("industry_cs", 1:5,
  c("Manufacturing", "Retail or trade", "Services", "Public sector", "Other"))

# ---- Section A: Respondent profile ----
sec_a <- sf_item("sec_a", "Section A: Respondent profile", type = "section_break",
  section_intro = "A few background questions about you.")
age <- sf_item("age", "Your age in years", type = "numeric")
gender <- sf_item("gender", "Your gender", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "gender_cs")
education <- sf_item("education", "Highest level of education completed", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "edu_cs")
job_role <- sf_item("job_role", "Your role or seniority", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "role_cs")
experience <- sf_item("experience", "Years of experience", type = "numeric")
industry <- sf_item("industry", "Your industry or sector", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "industry_cs")

# ---- Section B: Predictors and nominal outcome ----
sec_b <- sf_item("sec_b", "Section B: Predictors and nominal outcome", type = "section_break")
pred1_1 <- sf_item("pred1_1", "[Predictor 1 item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "pred1")
pred1_2 <- sf_item("pred1_2", "[Predictor 1 item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "pred1")
pred1_3 <- sf_item("pred1_3", "[Predictor 1 item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "pred1")
pred1 <- sf_scale("pred1", "Predictor 1", c("pred1_1", "pred1_2", "pred1_3"), method = "mean")
pred2_1 <- sf_item("pred2_1", "[Predictor 2 item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "pred2")
pred2_2 <- sf_item("pred2_2", "[Predictor 2 item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "pred2")
pred2_3 <- sf_item("pred2_3", "[Predictor 2 item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "pred2")
pred2 <- sf_scale("pred2", "Predictor 2", c("pred2_1", "pred2_2", "pred2_3"), method = "mean")
outcome_var <- sf_item("outcome_var", "[nominal outcome - replace]", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "out_cat")

# ---- Analysis plan (ids match the items and scales above) ----
plan_entry <- list(
  id                = "RQ1",
  research_question = "Which predictors distinguish the outcome categories?",
  family            = "prediction",
  method            = "regression_logistic_multinomial",
  roles             = list(
    predictors = c("pred1", "pred2"),
    dependent  = "outcome_var"
  ),
  options           = list(alpha = 0.05)
)

# ---- Assemble the instrument ----
instr <- sf_instrument(
  title         = "[Your study title]",
  description   = "[Population and purpose]",
  components    = list(
    sec_a, age, gender, education, job_role, experience, industry, sec_b, pred1_1, pred1_2, pred1_3, pred1, pred2_1, pred2_2, pred2_3, pred2, outcome_var
  ),
  analysis_plan = list(plan_entry)
)
